key_insight: A 3D physics-informed neural network couples patient-specific pulmonary blood flow with Windkessel outlet dynamics by separating basal pressure from smaller spatial pressure variations.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports meshless hemodynamic prediction and outlet-parameter estimation for patient-specific digital twins.
method: Embed flow equations and dynamic Windkessel (RCR) outlet conditions in PINN training.
Separate pressure components and enforce a Windkessel initial condition, pressure gauge, and global mass balance.
Use periodic Fourier time embedding to represent pulsatile flow.
evidence_signal: Tests on canonical 2D channels and a patient-specific right pulmonary artery showed flow-field errors on the order of data resolution; inverse estimation recovered three RCR parameters from synthetic data with about 0.3% error.
watch_item: Residual local-pressure biases remain, and robustness to noisy clinical data has not yet been established.
paper_title: A 3D PINN-Based Framework for Patient-Specific Pulmonary Hemodynamics Using Windkessel Models
